title: WfGg Radar operational discovery and controlled runtime evolution
problem: Extend the WfGg Radar UI session lifetime and add sliding renewal so long-running Autopilot monitoring does not require hourly reauthentication, without changing Last War token lifetime or weakening session security.
goals: Raise the Radar UI session TTL from 1 hour to the existing code maximum of 12 hours.
Add an authenticated same-origin session refresh endpoint that rotates the signed Radar session cookie without exposing or revalidating the Last War token.
Automatically renew the Radar UI session every 3 hours while the UI is active, and on return to a visible tab after a long pause.
Keep the server-side V6.19.4 Autopilot independent from the browser session so active discovery continues even if the UI session expires.
Preserve the encrypted Last War credential vault and all existing role/capability checks.
Use ChaCha DEV governance for qualification and production approval.
non_goals: Do not create a permanent Last War token or bypass Last War authentication expiry.
Do not persist a plaintext Last War token in the browser, Worker logs, jobs, Collector DB, VPS filesystem, or ChaCha DEV.
Do not modify the V6.19.4 connector or its Autopilot discovery logic.
Do not launch or stop any active Autopilot job as part of the session keepalive deployment.
Do not weaken same-origin mutation checks, role checks, or signed session verification.

current_change.purpose: Cloudflare Worker/UI-only change: 12-hour Radar UI sessions plus sliding renewal every 3 hours. Last War token lifetime and V6.19.4 connector runtime remain unchanged.

acceptance_criteria: The Worker session TTL is configured to 43200 seconds and remains capped at 12 hours.
POST /api/auth/session/refresh requires a valid existing Radar session and returns a rotated session cookie with the same identity and role.
The refresh endpoint never decrypts, validates, returns, or persists the Last War token.
The UI renews the Radar session every 3 hours while active and attempts renewal when returning to the visible tab after a long pause.
A 401 from the refresh endpoint stops keepalive and returns the UI to the normal login flow.
Logout stops keepalive and clears the Radar session as before.
V6.19.4 Autopilot jobs remain server-side and are not stopped or restarted by the session keepalive change.
No connector binary change is required.
Production deployment is explicit-approval gated and reversible.
architecture_invariants: GitHub stores code, branches, CI and release artifacts.
ChaCha DEV on ChaChaVPS is the runtime orchestrator.
ChaChaNas remains authoritative persistent storage for project data and backups.
VPS is runtime-oriented and not the authoritative durable project store.
Producer and verifier responsibilities remain separated.
